paper_title: Shuttle Between the Instructions and the Parameters of Large Language   Models
caption: : The induction performance of SHIP and SFT on SNI with respect to the number of observed samples. The accuracy is the average accuracy over all seen and unseen tasks.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the induction performance of two methods, SHIP and vanilla SFT, on the SNI benchmark as the number of observed samples increases from 1 to 6. The x-axis, labeled “observed samples,” is linear and ranges from 1 to 6 with integer tick marks. The y-axis, labeled “accuracy,” is also linear, ranging from 0.3 to 0.8 with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The green line with circular markers, representing SHIP, starts at approximately 0.81 at 1 observed sample, remains relatively stable around 0.80–0.81 through samples 2 to 3, dips slightly to about 0.79 at sample 4, then rises to 0.81 at sample 5 and 0.82 at sample 6. The blue line with circular markers, representing vanilla SFT, begins at approximately 0.33 at 1 observed sample, increases to 0.37 at sample 2, remains flat at 0.37 at sample 3, rises to 0.40 at sample 4, increases slightly to 0.41 at sample 5, and reaches 0.45 at sample 6. The legend in the lower right corner identifies the green line as “SHIP” and the blue line as “vanilla SFT.” The plot background includes a light gray grid to aid in reading values.
